subject.title: Adding ACP agent to agents.list silently hijacks all routing from implicit main agent

question: Should OpenClaw keep first-list-entry default routing and add warnings/doctor guidance, or change the default-selection contract so adding `agents.list` without `default: true` preserves implicit `main`?
rationale: The behavior is source-reproducible, but every viable fix intentionally changes documented routing semantics, config-write UX, or upgrade compatibility for multi-agent users.

options.title: Warn and guide
options.body: Keep the documented first-entry default behavior, but add config/doctor/CLI warnings and docs that make default displacement explicit before or after first `agents.list` writes.

options.title: Preserve implicit main
options.body: Change resolver or config normalization so implicit `main` remains default unless a listed agent is explicitly marked default, with migration and upgrade proof for existing configs.

options.title: Require explicit default
options.body: Reject or fail closed on non-empty `agents.list` without `default: true`, backed by doctor repair and compatibility messaging.

recommendation.title: Warn and guide
recommendation.body: Keep the documented first-entry default behavior, but add config/doctor/CLI warnings and docs that make default displacement explicit before or after first `agents.list` writes.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the original multi-agent routing policy and current carried-forward implementation points to steipete.
